findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition removes 4-arg API
findings.body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the max_width,max_height form now gets ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The resize/downsize refactor must support both arities, e.g. with splat args, not two methods with the same name.

findings.title: Stale tempfile.size causes unconditional 5x 80% downsizing
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 66 loops while tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. tempfile is an open File/Tempfile object modified in place by an external convert process in line 67. File#size on the open descriptor does not reliably reflect the new on-disk size, so the condition can stay true even after the file is already small enough. The result is up to 5 successive 80% resizes (~0.8^5 ~= 0.33 scale) degrading quality and wasting CPU when one pass would suffice. Use File.size(tempfile.path) re-stat after each pass and break when under limit.

findings.title: Downsize return value ignored and SVG/vector images corrupted
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) in a loop without checking its boolean return. If convert fails the code retries 4 more times then uploads the original oversized file anyway. Worse, the guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) which includes SVG, but OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly skips resizing SVG by just copying it because vector-to-raster convert with -resize/[0] mangles or fails on SVG. Downsizing SVG in place can corrupt it or needlessly rasterize it. Skip SVG and break on false return.

findings.title: Client max upload size hardcoded to 10MB ignoring SiteSetting
findings.body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js lines 182 and 246 replace Discourse.SiteSettings max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. This breaks admin configurability: instances with smaller or larger limits now validate against the wrong value client-side and show a wrong max_size_kb in the file_too_large error. A file rejected by the server will appear allowed locally and vice versa. Restore use of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypassing setting
findings.body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 55 changes FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...) to FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...). An admin who configured a small max_image_size_kb to bound bandwidth, disk and ImageMagick CPU can now be forced to download and process up to 10MB per API upload. The limit should remain derived from SiteSetting, with any headroom added explicitly, not a fixed 10MB.
